title: external-kms-plugin-and-cert-sync-controller-for-onprem-rotation
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: private installations need a way to integrate external KMS (cloud or on-prem HSM gateways) without forcing Vault-as-first-class and to keep TLS artifacts synchronized across namespaces during key rotation. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an optional installer hook that deploys a lightweight external-kms-plugin sidecar and Terraform snippets to register external KMS endpoints (KMS plugin config + policy templates); 2) a cert-sync-controller (Kubernetes controller) that watches KMS-backed key metadata and existing TLS secrets (including sealed-secrets-wrapped secrets) to perform automated, atomic certificate replacements across the cluster during rotation. Goals: reduce manual rotation steps for Private deployments, support customer-managed KMS/HSM, and provide a safe upgrade path with canaries and rollbacks. The description below outlines implementation details, migration plan, and risk mitigations. Implementation summary: - Installer/terraform: new optional module `external_kms` in terraform/ modules that wires up provider endpoints, validates TLS with provided CA bundle, and outputs Kubernetes Secret manifests for connector config. - Helm: chart changes add `externalKms.enabled` flag, sidecar container image references, RBAC rules for the cert-sync-controller, and a new `preupgrade` hook to validate existing TLS assets before applying new certs. - Controller: `cert-sync-controller` (Go) runs as a Deployment; it subscribes to a KMSConfig CRD and Secret events, uses signed key fingerprints to detect rotation candidates, generates CSR via local signer when allowed, and rotates target Secrets (supports sealed-secrets encrypted payloads by unlocking via the installer-provided sealing key). - Backwards compatibility: all changes are gated behind `externalKms.enabled=false` by default; controller is opt-in. - Rollout: default canary to 5% of nodes via nodeSelector + label-based canary, automated healthchecks (liveness/readiness + smoke requests) and automatic rollback on certificate validation failures. - Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration e2e in the benchmark-lab that exercises a simulated KMS gateway, and manual on-prem validation (steps included in docs). See release notes + upgrade instructions below. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with input/output docs - [x] Helm chart templates and hook - [x] CRD + controller implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Operator RBAC and PSP/PodSecurity verification - [x] Docs and upgrade guide - [x] Canary rollout strategy and rollback hooks Related: builds on work in ENG-4000 (vault auto-unseal) and complements sealed-secrets automation (does not replace Vault). Security: we require KMS endpoints to authenticate via mTLS or a signed token; the installer will validate CA bundles and refuses to enable the controller if authentication tests fail. For sealed-secrets, controller will only decrypt using cluster sealing key provided explicitly by the admin during install (no implicit key retrieval). Migration notes: - Upgrading from 2.3 -> 2.4: operator will detect existing TLS secrets and run a dry-run validation; admin must approve the first rotation via the console or CLI. - Rollback: chart includes helm hooks which will restore previous Secret manifests (helm rollback) and controller will stop rotating if `externalKms.enabled=false`. Observability: new metrics (redwood_cert_sync_rotations_total, redwood_cert_sync_errors, redwood_kms_plugin_sync_latency) and tracing spans (controller reconcile) added to console dashboards. Rollout plan: stage to Dedicated beta clusters for 2 weeks, then enable canary for 5% of customer on-prem clusters with customer opt-in, gather telemetry, then full release. See release_notes for more details.

release_notes:
- opt-in external KMS integration for Private installs (terraform + helm)
- cert-sync-controller to automate TLS secret rotation across namespaces (supports sealed-secrets)
- new metrics and dashboard panels for rotation observability
- upgrade notes and dry-run mode to validate before rotating
